references.text: God says to Israel: "You are my witnesses." Jesus uses similar language in [ref:Jes 43:10|Isaiah 43:10] when he appoints the disciples as witnesses to his suffering, death, and resurrection – a role that mirrors Israel's calling to testify about the Lord's deeds.

In [ref:Jes 43:12|Isaiah 43:12] the Lord says: "You are my witnesses." This repeated formulation from Isaiah forms the background for Jesus' sending of the disciples as witnesses to the climax of salvation history.

In [ref:Apg 1:8|Acts 1:8] the risen Jesus repeats the promise that the disciples will be his witnesses "to the ends of the earth" – a direct continuation of the commission in Luke 24:48, now linked to the power of the Holy Spirit.
In [ref:Apg 2:32|Acts 2:32] Peter declares on Pentecost: "This Jesus God raised up, and we are all witnesses of it." This is the fulfillment of the witness commission Jesus gave in Luke 24:48.
Peter calls himself and the other apostles "witnesses" to Jesus' resurrection in [ref:Apg 3:15|Acts 3:15], thereby carrying out the commission Jesus gave them.
In [ref:Apg 5:32|Acts 5:32] the apostles say to the Council: "We are witnesses of these things," a direct parallel to Jesus' words that the disciples are witnesses.

In [ref:Apg 10:39-41|Acts 10:39–41] Peter testifies in Cornelius' house that they are witnesses to everything Jesus did, and that they ate and drank with him after the resurrection – exactly the witness commission Jesus gave them.
Paul refers in [ref:Apg 13:31|Acts 13:31] to those who followed Jesus from Galilee to Jerusalem, and who are now his witnesses to the people – a confirmation of the witness role from Luke 24:48.

In [ref:Joh 15:27|John 15:27] Jesus says: "You also will be witnesses, because you have been with me from the beginning." This is a parallel to Jesus' appointment of the disciples as witnesses in Luke 24:48.
In [ref:1 Pet 5:1|1 Peter 5:1] Peter refers to himself as "a witness of Christ's sufferings," pointing to the personal fulfillment of the witness commission Jesus gave in Luke 24:48.
